title: Tenant chain-of-custody ledger and retention evidence harvester for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background:
We need a defensible, machine-readable chain-of-custody (CoC) ledger and a retention-evidence harvester for Dedicated tenants. Current residency attestations are generated ad-hoc and lack a canonical timeline that ties tenant traffic, node assignments, retention policy changes, and exported evidence together for auditors. This ticket scopes an automated pipeline that collects relevant telemetry, produces signed ledger entries for each custody-affecting event, and bundles retention proof artifacts for export (S3, signed tarball).

Goal:
1) Implement a lightweight CoC ledger service that records custody events (node assignment, VM reboots, block storage attachment/detachment, backup snapshots, retention policy mutations) for Dedicated tenant namespaces.
2) Produce per-tenant evidence bundles that map to retention policy snapshots and include signed logs, manifests, and hash digests for tamper-evidence.
3) Integrate ledger signing with the existing key-rotation mechanism and produce human-readable and machine-consumable attestations for audits.

Scope (in-scope):
- Event capture from orchestration plane (k8s node annotations, scheduler events), storage layer (snapshot/backup events), and our serving runtime (tenant-route binds).
- Ledger entries schema, signed with sigstore-like signing flow using Redwood KMS wrapper.
- Evidence harvester that produces export bundles and an index.json manifest containing checksums and ledger references.
- Expose an API for auditors to request a time-windowed proof and for Console to surface evidence links.

Out-of-scope:
- Long-term archival policy (this will be a follow-up for retention tiering).
- Full legal contract wording for attestations (product-on-boarding will handle customer-specific agreements).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ledger service accepts and stores custody events and returns a signed reference ID (string) for each event.
2) Evidence harvester can generate a tenant export.zip that contains: index.json, ledger-refs.ndjson, signed-manifest.json, and cryptographic digests for each object.
3) Export bundles validate against the signing public key and index checksums.
4) Console link (internal-only) can fetch the latest export for a tenant and show status.
5) Unit and integration tests cover event ingestion, signing, and bundle generation.
proposed_solution:
Architecture summary:
- custody-ledger-service: lightweight HTTP service (golang) with append-only ledger stored in CockroachDB (range-partitioned by tenant) and backed by WAL S3 for replay. Each ledger record contains event_type, timestamp, tenant_id, node_id, actor, metadata, and parent_ref.
- signing-agent: sidecar process running in the control plane that requests ephemeral signing tokens from KMS and signs ledger blocks; it also publishes verifyable public keys to a well-known location.
- harvester-worker: scheduled job that collects logs/manifests for a given tenant/time-window and creates export bundles; bundles are uploaded to a restricted S3 bucket and an entry written to the audit-index table.
- API endpoints: POST /v1/ledger/events, GET /v1/ledger/{tenant}/exports?from=...&to=..., and /v1/ledger/verify/{export_id}.

Trade-offs considered:
- DB choice: CockroachDB gives strong consistency and geo-partitioning for dedicated regions; alternative (Dynamo/Cassandra) would complicate multi-region proofs.
- Signing strategy: using short-lived KMS-derived signing tokens reduces risk vs granting long-lived signing keys to control plane services.
- Storage of bundles: keeping bundles in a dedicated S3 project bucket with object lock for a configurable retention window is preferred for auditability, but increases cost; we'll enable object lock as an opt-in per-tenant flag.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Canary, 2 weeks):
- Deploy custody-ledger-service to staging and one dedicated-tenant trial region.
- Run signing-agent with test keys and validate signed ledger entries.
- Harvest one-week worth of events for trial tenant and validate bundle integrity.

Phase 2 (Beta, 4 weeks):
- Enable for small set of Dedicated customers as beta (opt-in).
- Add Console UI link and API throttling/quotas.
- Gather feedback and performance metrics.

Phase 3 (GA):
- Turn on for all Dedicated tenants with notification and doc updates.
- Add retention-tiering follow-ups and legal templates.

Rollback plan: disable harvester jobs and revoke signing tokens; keep ledger read-only to preserve evidence while investigating.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for ledger ingestion, signature verification, and manifest generation.
- Integration test: simulate node attach/detach and verify ledger chain links (parent_ref) and export bundle correctness.
- Chaos test: force signing-agent restart and ensure ledger remains consistent after replay from WAL.
- Load test: ingest 10k events/min to validate write latency under expected Dedicated peak.
- Audit test: external verifier (script) validates an exported bundle against published public keys.
notes:
Security considerations:
- Signing-agent must run in a hardened control-plane namespace with minimal network permissions.
- All export bundles are access-controlled and logged.
- Consider HSM-backed root signing for GA.

Observability:
- Add per-tenant SLO for ledger write latency and harvester success rate.
- Trace events through distributed tracing (W3C traceparent) and include trace_id in ledger metadata.

Open questions:
- Should parent_ref be strictly monotonic per-tenant or allow parallel chains per node? Preferring monotonic for simpler proofs but may require sequence reservation under high concurrency.
- Opt-in vs opt-out for object lock on S3 exports.

comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Kumar: Created ticket and initial design sketch. Dropped prototype notes into Confluence. Assigned to Diego for initial spike.

2025-02-17 - Diego Morales: Spike complete. Verified event sources in staging (k8s scheduler + runtime bind events). Observed ~120 events/hour for trial tenant; design updated to use batch append to reduce DB contention.
2025-02-19 - Security review (Joan Lee): Reviewed signing flow; requested HSM consideration and key use audits added to the plan. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-02-22 - Diego Morales: Implemented ledger schema and basic POST /v1/ledger/events endpoint. Pushed initial branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/compare/ledger-proto. Added unit tests for signature packing.

2025-02-25 - PM review (Rafael Singh): Confirmed acceptance criteria align with compliance ask. PM requested export manifest include human-readable timeline summary for auditors; added to manifest schema.

2025-02-28 - Diego Morales: Began harvester worker implementation and integration tests. Noted a race where node reassign + snapshot events can generate out-of-order timestamps; proposing to introduce event_seq per-tenant to guarantee ordering.
NEXT: implement event_seq reservation and update harvester to produce index.json with timeline summary. Schedule canary deploy for 2025-03-03.
